_note: Documentation for each certification probe and each section.

sections.Symmetry & invariance: Identities that follow from the symmetry group of space and from the indistinguishability of identical particles. The exact potential energy surface satisfies them for any configuration.
sections.Self-consistency: Identities that relate a model's own output heads to each other: forces to the energy gradient, stress to the strain derivative, the Hessian to itself. A model whose heads are trained separately has no structural reason to satisfy them.
sections.Statistical mechanics: Equilibrium relations that hold for any conservative potential sampled at temperature T. They probe the dynamics a model generates rather than a single static configuration.
sections.Regularity: Smoothness of the fitted surface. Energy jumps, force kinks, spurious minima and tortuosity are properties of the fit rather than of the underlying physics.

equivariance.title: Equivariance
equivariance.identity: E(R x) = E(x) and F(R x) = R F(x) for every rotation R.
equivariance.catches: Rotational invariance of the energy and equivariance of the forces.
equivariance.why: The defect is the residual after rotating the substrate through a set of random rotations. Non-equivariant architectures, neighbour lists truncated to a fixed count, and orientation-dependent preprocessing can all contribute.

parity.title: Parity
parity.identity: The stress is even under improper operations: sigma(P x) = P sigma(x) P^T.
parity.catches: Reflection and inversion behaviour of the stress.
parity.why: Separates improper symmetry from pure rotation, so a model can pass the rotation test and still show a residual here.

representation.title: Representation
representation.identity: E is extensive, invariant under a change of unit cell describing the same crystal, and invariant under permutation of identical atoms.
representation.catches: Extensivity, lattice-gauge and egg-box dependence, permutation sensitivity.
representation.why: Supercelling, re-choosing lattice vectors for the same crystal, and relabelling identical atoms should leave the energy per atom unchanged. Grid-based or cutoff-sensitive representations tend to show an egg-box residual.

trimer.title: Trimer
trimer.identity: Three-body symmetry of an equilateral trimer, and antisymmetry of the force Jacobian in the transverse channel.
trimer.catches: Many-body symmetry, three-body coupling at range, transverse non-conservativeness.
trimer.why: A radial conservativeness scan cannot see a purely transverse (curl) force. The transverse channel here is a matrix-free Jacobian-antisymmetry test covering that direction. The three-body channel needs isolated fragments, which some models decline to evaluate.

zero_modes.title: Zero modes
zero_modes.identity: The Hessian has the zero modes required by translation and rotation, and obeys the acoustic sum rule.
zero_modes.catches: Rotational and translational zero-mode residuals, acoustic-sum-rule violation, imaginary modes.
zero_modes.why: Rigid translation and rigid rotation cost no energy, so the corresponding Hessian eigenvalues should vanish. A residual shows up in Gamma-point phonons.

conservativeness.title: Conservativeness
conservativeness.catches: Agreement between the reported force and the energy gradient.
conservativeness.why: A fourth-order finite difference of the energy along a scan, compared against the model's own force. Scope note: a purely transverse force is invisible to a one-dimensional radial scan, which is what the trimer probe covers.

betti.title: Maxwell-Betti
betti.identity: The response of atom i to a displacement of atom j equals the response of j to i, that is, the Hessian is symmetric.
betti.why: A force field derived from an energy has a symmetric Hessian by Clairaut's theorem, so a residual indicates the forces are not a single energy's gradient.

cross_maxwell.title: Cross-Maxwell
cross_maxwell.identity: The mixed second derivative of E with respect to strain and position is the same whether it is reached through the force head or the stress head.
cross_maxwell.catches: Agreement between the force and stress heads on the internal-strain block.
cross_maxwell.why: The internal-strain coupling enters elastic constants and phonon-strain coupling. Two separately trained heads need not agree on it.

reversibility.title: Reversibility
reversibility.identity: A velocity-Verlet NVE trajectory run forward and then backward returns to its starting state.
reversibility.why: Velocity-Verlet is time-reversible for any smooth position-dependent force, so this measures roughness rather than smooth non-conservativeness. The energy-drift slope is reported separately.

stress_consistency.title: Stress consistency
stress_consistency.catches: Agreement between the stress head and the energy gradient.
stress_consistency.why: Also sensitive to unit conventions: a stress reported in GPa rather than eV/A^3 appears as a residual of the conversion factor.

config_temperature.title: Configurational temperature
config_temperature.identity: The configurational temperature <|F|^2> / <div F> equals the kinetic temperature at equilibrium.
config_temperature.catches: Conservativeness, measured from the dynamics rather than from a static configuration.
config_temperature.why: The identity holds for any conservative potential in equilibrium. The estimator is a finite-sample average, so it does not reach machine precision even for an exact potential.

equipartition.title: Equipartition
equipartition.identity: Every quadratic mode carries kT/2 at equilibrium.
equipartition.catches: Agreement between Hessian curvature and the amplitude a mode explores in MD, resolved per mode.
equipartition.why: Because it is mode-resolved, the spread across modes carries as much information as the mean. Soft modes show up here first.

virial.title: Virial
virial.identity: The Clausius virial -<sum r . F> / 2 equals the internal kinetic energy at equilibrium.
virial.catches: Equilibrium consistency without using the Hessian.
virial.why: A Hessian-free check, so its sensitivity differs from equipartition's. Long-range and boundary handling enter here.

smoothness.title: Smoothness
smoothness.identity: The exact surface is smooth, so an energy profile along a path has no jumps, force kinks or spurious extrema.
smoothness.catches: Energy jumps, force kinks, spurious minima, tortuosity.
smoothness.why: Scored from the roughness of the path rather than from a single algebraic identity, which is why its target is given as a score.
